7. Choice under Uncertainty

From expected utility through the measurement of risk aversion to the demand for insurance — choice in the face of uncertain prospects.

  • Expected Utility — A lottery LLL is worth the expectation of Bernoulli utility, U(L)=∑pnu(xn)U(L) = \sum p_n u(x_n)U(L)=∑pn​u(xn​). See the Jensen gap between the expected value and expected utility on a concave utility curve.
  • Measuring Risk Aversion — Raise the risk-aversion coefficient γ\gammaγ in CRRA utility and the certainty equivalent drifts away from the expected value — the risk premium grows. The Arrow-Pratt measure reads off alongside.
  • Demand for Insurance — The contingent-claims diagram: wealth in the loss state vs the no-loss state. At a fair premium the optimum is full insurance on the 45-degree line — loading on the premium slides it to partial insurance.
